title: VERY mediocre at best - read here before paying
body: The app has a clean and modern interface, but beyond that, it feels extremely lackluster for something that requires a paid subscription. If you only want to casually listen to ATC and pilot communications, it may be entertaining. But if you actually expect reliable features and value for your money, this app is honestly hard to recommend. I was curious to listen to four flights I was on in the last two months ago, and there was essentially nothing available for all four. That is honestly unacceptable for a paid aviation app advertising playback functionality. If it cannot reliably provide audio from flights within the last 60 days, what exactly are people paying for? At this point, the app feels like a slightly glorified version of using LiveATC alongside Flightradar24 except those services are either free or offer far more value. Charging premium pricing for such limited functionality feels unjustified. Overall, disappointing experience and absolutely not worth the money.

title: Fun, but some faults
body: Tried using this during a flight today. It was fun, but the interface (while pretty) has major UX problems. I won't get too deep into things that are confusing to find (e.g. like how to move the map, you have to tap it first apparently; or how hard it is to read the text transcription over the map), but there are other annoying things. In particular, it's very difficult to use if you're flying and want to keep up with your flight. For instance if you're tracking your own flight on the map, it's way too easy to tap out of it and it re-centers to the airport itself and good luck finding your flight again, because searching for it won't even show it on the map. And it doesn't always switch to the right controller, for instance it kept my flight in approach control even though it was obviously tower during the final landing and I missed the real-time tower calls. And even if you search the app for your flight, it doesn't show it on a map a or have live voice at all, just a chat-style log that often attributes the wrong party speaking (eg showing the plane speaking instead of the controller quite often). You can't even tap on the controller they're showing to switch to their frequency in this view. There's basically no coverage further outside of approach/departure so most of your flight, ATC is not available. Not entirely sure this is all ATC App's fault though. Also it's $90 for an annual subscription which is kinda nuts if you're just curious when you're flying. There's a week-long option, but it's still over $5 and you have to remember to cancel. I'd love to just buy cheap access to the flight I'm on, would happily pay $2 or so. It's probably a better deal for 24-hour aviation nerds or people learning ATC-speak. But the idea is cool and the interface is very pretty (if not hard to use). The real-time transcriptions, highlighting the relevant airplane (usually), and incident playbacks are all very neat and I'm sure was difficult to get this right. TL;DR: make it easier to track a particular flight and provide better options for casual users please.

title: Honest review: future potential
body: This app has the potential to be a game changer. The pros: It does a great job of showing which pilots are talking on the map. The transcript feature is awesome. I also enjoyed the rewind feature. The notifications of incidents is awesome as well. The cons: I decided to track my wife’s flight and listen to the pilots on flight. I could hear departure and then it went silent for 2 hours and then I heard ~20min before arrival. Why is that? Because this app doesn’t have any ARTCC section or zone coverages. Also, there are still a lot of airports that aren’t covered here. Also the price is another con. Hard to justify the price for something I can do on other apps for free. This app would be a game changer if I could click on a specific flight and listen all the way from departure to arrival. Yes this is a huge undertaking to make happen. Figure out how to make it so the user doesn’t have to switch frequencies like on other apps. NOW if this app could do this, it’d be well worth the money.

There needs to be a way to bypass it if you don’t want to waste time and figure it out yourself. Also, the pricing model on this is very predatory. $90 a year or $7 a week. There needs to be a middle ground, and even then this is a lot. Yes I know there is a free trial. That’s how I have been trying it out, but unfortunately I don’t see myself paying for this. If you’re gonna be charging that much money, this app needs to have the functionality of ADS-B exchange and Flight Radar built in. Airport pins on the map, arrival and departure boards, all that stuff. Not just the explore mode where you move around a map with limited functions. Oh and one more thing. It’s not cool to keep playing the radio communications in the background after you return to the Home Screen on your phone. There needs to be an option to disable that feature added. All in all. This is the right idea, it’s a cool concept, I really hope this can gain some more functionality in the future and be a one stop shop for aviation. Because Flight Radar 24 has literally gone down the drain. You have a great opportunity to capitalize it!

title: Some things you need to know.
body: Judging by most reviews, this is a terrific app, even if it is very expensive: $90 per year. If you intend to download it, there are some things you should know. 1. You can opt for a seven-day trial period, BUT you will need to enter your credit card AND billing will automatically start when the trial period is over, if you don't--or forget to--cancel. Put a reminder on your calendar! 2. The app has limitations. If you are familiar with the Air Traffic Control (ATC) system in the U.S., you will understand those limitations and why they exist. To explain this in a ridiculously simple way, ATC has two parts. One is the airport environment and the other is the rest of the U.S. airspace, the enroute environment. This app only tracks traffic and communication in the airport environment. It would be nearly impossible for it to track communication beyond that, because the enroute environment comprises hundreds of sectors, each with its own set of frequencies. While there are many apps that can track aircraft in the enroute environment, there will probably never be an app that can track all the communication that takes place between flight crews and controllers there. All the different frequency changes through all the sectors that aircraft pass through as they navigate from one airport to another would be nearly impossible to follow without some very expensive infrastructure. Bottom line: This app is not perfect, but it does a pretty good job following aircraft in the immediate airport environments of the airports that are covered. The recording feature is great, as you can go back and replay communications between ATC and specific airplanes. This feature also is not perfect, but it's pretty good. Is the app worth $90 a year? You have to decide that for yourself. I've signed up for one year. Time will tell...

title: I am basically a pilot now
body: Look, I downloaded this app as a joke to feel important while waiting for my delayed Spirit flight. Three hours later, I’m emotionally invested in Delta 472’s approach into Atlanta and genuinely stressed about a Cessna doing pattern work in Wisconsin. This app has ruined me in the best way possible. I now speak in callsigns. I’ve said “roger” to my wife unironically. I know what a “heavy” is. My coworkers think I’ve lost my mind because I keep muttering “cleared for the visual two-eight left” during meetings. The real-time transcription is chef’s kiss. Finally, I can understand what those pilots are saying instead of just hearing “mxfrghble wind shear mxfrghble maintain flight level.” 250+ airports?? I’ve listened to controllers at airports I will never visit for reasons I cannot explain. It’s 2am and I’m checking if anyone’s landing at Boise. Someone is. I’m invested now. If you’ve ever wanted to feel the vicarious thrill of aviation without any of the responsibility, training, or FAA oversight, this is your app. My screen time report is horrifying and I regret nothing. Cleared to download, runway app store, winds calm.
